summary.text: Dione Sims is a software quality development director, community organizer and nonprofit founder who won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.5% of the vote. She describes herself as a granddaughter of Dr. Opal Lee and says she is running on living wages, public schools and an economy that works for working people.

paragraphs.text: Graduated from Southwest High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Texas Wesleyan University in 1989, according to Ballotpedia.
Works in information technology; in her Candidate Connection survey she describes herself as a software quality development director who has led diverse teams of professionals.
Describes herself as the president and founder of a nonprofit focused on unity, understanding and social justice.

Describes herself as the granddaughter of Dr. Opal Lee, whom she calls the Grandmother of Juneteenth. Says she has co-produced the Annual Juneteenth Fort Worth Celebration since 2015 and helped lead the Opal's Walk campaign for national Juneteenth recognition.
Says she has served on several boards, and lists endorsements from Fort Worth officials and the Fort Worth Association of Federated Women's Club.
Defeated William Marks in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 60.5% to 39.5%, to become the party's nominee against Rep. Williams.
